screenshots.title: Codex requests a workspace-scoped command approval
screenshots.caption: The live Android session pauses before creating the requested Tetris folder and files, showing the exact command and selected remote workspace.

screenshots.title: Codex requests file-change approval
screenshots.caption: After the directory is created, Codex requests a second approval before writing the three Tetris source files.
screenshots.alt: Codex file change approval in the Android SSH session

screenshots.title: Codex completes and verifies the Tetris app
screenshots.caption: Codex created index.html, styles.css, and app.js in /home/agent/temp/android-e2e-codex-tetris, then verified their presence and checked app.js syntax before the Android session reached Complete.
screenshots.alt: Completed Codex Android SSH session after creating and verifying a Tetris app

screenshots.title: OpenCode session ready · real emulator run
screenshots.caption: The rebuilt APK connected to agent@void over SSH, verified the saved local credential, and opened the native OpenCode ACP session.

screenshots.title: OpenCode is building · real emulator run
screenshots.caption: The prompt reached the remote backend and the Android activity stream shows mkdir and write tool calls while the agent works in /home/agent/temp.
screenshots.alt: OpenCode remote agent creating files in the selected workspace

screenshots.title: OpenCode completes the coding task
screenshots.caption: OpenCode created tetris-session/index.html, ran file and game-board smoke checks, and the Android session reached Complete.
screenshots.alt: Completed OpenCode coding session on the remote workspace

screenshots.title: OpenCode completes the latest Tetris build
screenshots.caption: In the latest emulator run, OpenCode created /home/agent/temp/android-e2e-tetris/index.html, styles.css, and app.js, then verified the folder contents with ls before the Android session reached Complete.
screenshots.alt: OpenCode Android SSH session complete after creating a Tetris web app

screenshots.title: Claude Code sign-in is required
screenshots.caption: The CLI is installed, but claude auth status reported loggedIn=false, so Android shows the visual sign-in checklist instead of opening a session.

screenshots.title: Claude Code chooses an account method
screenshots.caption: The live remote CLI is installed but unauthenticated. Android relays the initial account-method choice, while the later browser handoff stays off the gallery because it contains ephemeral authorization data.
screenshots.alt: Claude Code account-method choice in the Android SSH setup flow

screenshots.title: Claude requests an Android approval before writing
screenshots.caption: The real SSH session pauses before writing index.html in /home/agent/temp/claude-e2e-tetris, showing the selected workspace and an explicit approve or reject action.
screenshots.alt: Claude Code write approval in the Android SSH session

screenshots.title: Claude requests verification approval
screenshots.caption: After creating the Tetris source files, Claude requests approval to list the folder and syntax-check game.js before reporting completion.
screenshots.alt: Claude Code verification approval in the Android SSH session

screenshots.title: Claude completes the remote Tetris app
screenshots.caption: Claude created index.html, style.css, and game.js in /home/agent/temp/claude-e2e-tetris. The Android session reached Complete and the remote JavaScript syntax check passed.
screenshots.alt: Completed Claude Code Android SSH session after creating and verifying a Tetris app

screenshots.title: Antigravity offers secure sign-in
screenshots.caption: The installed Antigravity CLI is waiting for Google OAuth or a Google Cloud project. The Android app keeps the browser authorization code out of recorded evidence.
screenshots.alt: Antigravity sign-in method choice in the Android SSH setup flow

screenshots.title: Antigravity completes a Tetris website in the selected workspace
screenshots.caption: The real Android SSH session created index.html, styles.css, and app.js in /home/agent/temp/antigravity-e2e-tetris-v3. Antigravity then ran node --check app.js and the session reached Complete.
screenshots.alt: Completed Antigravity Android SSH session after creating and verifying a Tetris website
